questions.prompt: In MCP, what does the host do for each server it connects to?

options.text: It runs the server itself, so a server can never live on someone else's computer
options.explanation: A server can run locally or remotely. The host does not have to run it.

options.text: It shares one client between all servers to save memory and reduce the number of links
options.explanation: Each server gets its own client with a dedicated connection.

options.text: It creates one MCP client for each server, and each client keeps its own connection
options.explanation: Right. The architecture page says the host creates one MCP client for each MCP server.

questions.prompt: What does Anthropic's MCP connector (beta) support from the MCP feature set?

options.text: Only tool calls, at the time of the doc, so a server's other features are not used
options.explanation: Right. The page says only tool calls are currently supported.

options.text: Every feature in the MCP specification, because the connector is a full MCP client
options.explanation: The page lists a limit. Only tool calls are supported.

options.text: Only local STDIO servers, which is the reason the connector runs on the studio's laptop
options.explanation: The reverse is true. Local STDIO servers cannot be connected directly.

questions.prompt: In which direction does OpenAI's Secure MCP Tunnel open its connection?

options.text: Inbound, from OpenAI into the private network, through a port the studio opens
options.explanation: The tunnel is made so that no inbound firewall ports are needed.

options.text: Outbound, from a host inside your own network to an OpenAI-hosted MCP endpoint
options.explanation: Right. OpenAI describes an outbound-only connection from a host inside your network.

options.text: Both ways at once, so the studio must open the firewall in each direction to use it
options.explanation: It is outbound-only. Nothing needs to be opened inbound.
